subject.title: [Bug]: Secret provider crash-loop exhausts 1Password service account rate limits

question: Should gateway startup keep fail-fast SecretRef activation, add a bounded generic retry/degraded-startup policy, or introduce user-configurable retry/circuit-breaker behavior for exec secret providers?
rationale: This changes how OpenClaw handles unavailable credentials at startup and can trade off fail-closed security against availability and external account-wide rate-limit protection.

options.title: Bounded Generic Startup Policy
options.body: Add a small maintainer-owned startup backoff/degraded behavior for repeated SecretRef failures without hardcoding 1Password or adding broad new config first.

options.title: Docs And Plugin Delegation
options.body: Keep startup fail-fast and document supervisor restart limits plus external batching/caching resolvers such as the linked Varlock 1Password plugin.

options.title: Configurable Retry Policy
options.body: Add a public retry/circuit-breaker config surface with migration-safe docs and tests, accepting the extra configuration contract.

recommendation.title: Bounded Generic Startup Policy
recommendation.body: Add a small maintainer-owned startup backoff/degraded behavior for repeated SecretRef failures without hardcoding 1Password or adding broad new config first.

likelyOwner.reason: joshavant has the strongest feature-history signal for provider-based external secrets and eager SecretRef runtime activation.
